_notes: Keycloak OIDC (realm masar, client masar-dashboard, Authorization Code + PKCE). The direct
password grant is disabled, so the real form has to be driven.
Step 2 settles the race between 'the login form appeared' and 'we were already signed in
via the SSO cookie'. `goto` resolves on domcontentloaded, before Keycloak renders, so
without it every onlyIfVisible step below sees nothing, skips, and the flow finishes still
sitting on the auth page having done nothing. The selector lists both outcomes and the
runner takes the first match.
THE LAST TWO STEPS SWITCH THE UI TO ENGLISH, AND THEY MATTER.
The dashboard is bilingual and DEFAULTS TO ARABIC (dir=rtl, lang=ar). The choice is kept in
localStorage under `lang`, which Playwright's storageState captures - so switching here, once,
in the cached login state, means every spec that reuses that state starts in English. Verified:
a fresh context built from the saved state opens /shipments with dir=ltr and lang=en.
Doing it per-spec instead would be both slower and unreliable, since a spec that forgot would
silently look for English text on an Arabic page and fail somewhere unrelated to its subject.
Every step is onlyIfVisible so the flow is idempotent: run against an already-authenticated
session, or one already in English, and it becomes a no-op rather than an error.
The final waitForVisible is the assertion. Once English is active the toggle reads AR, so
seeing an AR button is proof the switch actually happened rather than a hope that it did.
The steps before the language switch dismiss a PRODUCTION-ACCESS DISCLAIMER modal
("Authorized Access Only...") that appears on login. It is a real modal backdrop, so it
intercepts every click underneath - including the EN toggle. Left in place it does not fail
with 'modal is open'; it fails with a click timeout on whatever the test tried to press next,
which is a much harder thing to diagnose.
THERE ARE THREE ACKNOWLEDGEMENTS, AND ALL THREE ARE REQUIRED.
The modal's Accept button is bound to `disabled: !allConsentsGiven()`, where allConsentsGiven
is termsAccepted && privacyAccepted && consentFormAccepted. An earlier version of this file
clicked a single `input[type=checkbox]` selector - and because login-runner.ts calls .first()
on every click locator, that ticked ONE of the three and left Accept permanently disabled.
The failure surfaced as a click timeout on the EN toggle underneath the still-open backdrop.
The three boxes are PrimeNG p-checkbox components with stable inputIds
(disclaimer-consent-terms / -privacy / -form). We click their <label for=...> rather than the
inputs themselves: PrimeNG visually hides the real input behind a styled box, and a label
click is the native, reliable way to toggle it. The component resets all three to false every
time the modal opens, so there is no partial state to inherit from a previous run.
ON 2FA: THE OTP REQUIREMENT WAS REMOVED FROM THE DEVSIM ACCOUNTS ON 2026-09-08.
Until then every live account (janssen2@masar.com, and the admin) answered the password step
with a One-time code prompt, which no declarative step can satisfy -- auth.setup.ts timed out
and wrote EMPTY_STATE every run. It is gone now, verified by this flow completing unattended,
so the normal path works again and specs use stateFor('<slug>').
If it ever comes back, the fallback is already built rather than needing rediscovery:
node automation-hub/scripts/capture-state.mjs --portal <slug> --role admin
writes .auth/<slug>-<role>.json, which auth.setup.ts does not own and cannot overwrite, and
lib/captured-state.ts reads it with an actionable error when it is missing or stale. An admin
capture is also mirrored onto .auth/<slug>.json so existing projects keep working.
